 George had a long walk to take, and when he got back it was dark. As he reached the garden gate, he remembered what his uncle had said that morning about Watch. "Now," he said to himself, "I'll see if I can get into the house without Master Watch knowing. If I can’t, he is smarter than I think." So George took off his shoes and walked quietly on the soft grass, looking like a thief, until he reached the wide gravel path that he had to cross to get to the back of the house. He paused for a minute, looking for Watch, and soon saw him lying near the front door with his black nose on his white paws, fast asleep. George carefully stepped onto the gravel path, one foot at a time. As he did, Watch’s ears pricked up, but because it was dark, George didn’t see them.
